svg.aria-label: How to write ળ: one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
svg.title: Writing ળ
svg.desc: 1 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ળ (gujarati), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ળ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source note on variation: The teaching app animates ળ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper left, circles around the broad left bowl, rises through the narrow middle turn, crosses the high right arch, then descends the tall right spine into its lower foot without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the broad bowl, narrow middle turn, high arch, tall spine, and lower foot, but its printed body is wider and more angular and its spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's left-bowl-to-middle-turn-to-right-spine order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the bowl, turn, arch, spine, foot, and terminals differently.
svg.text: How it is written — one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
